items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: Bix and I went over to Paul and said, 'Why don't you come up on the stand, and conduct the band?'

ctx.x: From Philadelphia. They were appearing in Philadelphia at a theatre and I guess after the last show they came down, had enough time. We were very happy to see them, of course, and it was an event. So we got talking between sets and Bix and I went over to Paul and said, 'Why don't you come up on the stand, and conduct the band?' 'I don't know any of the arrangements,' he said. 'You don't have to know the arrangements, beat lead off and the band plays, that's all.' Okay.

He comes up on the stand and he goes off, in the way -- Lawrence Welk all over, a-one and a-two, you know, I think that's where Welk got it. But he used to clown around a lot and he starts that off, 'What will we play?' so they start off with something, I forget, I think it was a thing called 'Sorry,' where the band starts off like a shotgun. Chauncey used to start it off with a revolver, bang, on a rimshot and it was one of Quicksell's tunes.
